core_claim.P: Oracle extension stores Counts[tokenA] at slot uint256(uint160(tokenA)) and Snapshots at slot (uint256(uint160(tokenB)) << 32) | i in the same 256-bit storage key space, and expandCapacity is fully permissionless with no access control, no ERC20 validation, and no oracle pool existence check
core_claim.I: Snapshot writes must not overwrite another token's Counts entry, and expandCapacity must not allow unprivileged callers to corrupt Counts storage for arbitrary tokens
core_claim.V: An attacker can pick (tokenB, i) such that the snapshot slot equals Counts[tokenA]'s slot, then call oracle.expandCapacity(tokenB, i+1) so the loop's sstore((tokenB << 32) | i, 1) overwrites Counts[tokenA], enabling DoS of any oracle pool

distinct_impacts.description: Attacker can overwrite another token's Counts entry via a crafted expandCapacity call, corrupting the Counts storage for that token
Denial of service of any oracle pool, triggered on subsequent pool operations (swap, deposit, withdraw) that call maybeInsertSnapshot
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: Oracle storage slot collision allows DoS of any oracle pool via `expandCapacity`
